agenda.title: Reconstruction fidelity baseline
agenda.description: Establish a baseline battery for Agent Pretorius before any additional self-development. Record voice, decision patterns, uncertainty handling, relationship reasoning, and research behavior without reading expected answers during execution.

agenda.title: LoRA lineage audit
agenda.description: Compare the archived LoRA dataset versions and document what character traits, voice corrections, and prompt diversity changed across versions. Do not promote generated conclusions to canon without evidence.

agenda.title: Autobiography gap reconstruction plan
agenda.description: Inventory what the current resource archive can and cannot establish about the canonical Pretorius developmental history. Produce a gap map that distinguishes known facts, inferred material, and missing source documents.

agenda.title: Model portability trial design
agenda.description: Design a controlled test that runs the same Agent Pretorius persistent state across at least two compatible language-model substrates and measures continuity of decisions, voice, memory, relationships, and research goals.

agenda.title: Blinded trace evaluator validation
agenda.description: Validate the blind-trace workflow using synthetic source labels before it is used on experimental Pretorius. Confirm that source metadata cannot leak into the evaluator packet and that judgments are frozen before unblinding.

agenda.title: Relationship continuity test
agenda.description: Create a non-leading test for whether relationship judgments reflect accumulated shared history rather than immediate dialogue sentiment. Preserve evidence and contradictory observations.

agenda.title: Self-model calibration study
agenda.description: Compare Agent Pretorius self-model claims with independently logged actions over time. Identify claims that are supported, contradicted, or too vague to test.

agenda.title: Always-on drift monitor
agenda.description: Use the continuity prompt battery to collect longitudinal snapshots. Track changes after model swaps, memory growth, LoRA changes, or architecture changes without assuming that stability is always desirable.
